correctness.rationale: Cyclic geometric monodromy follows from tame inertia and Riemann–Hurwitz; deck subgroup projection is Frobenius equivariant and injective because translations act freely. Exact supersingular Weierstrass automorphism equations show Frobenius invariance forces r=0 or u and excludes a=1; a=0 has two valid stable order-three subgroups and the explicit tame y-cover. Ordinary automorphism groups have no element of order three; five F2 isomorphism classes exhaust the scope. The GF16 program exactly reproduces the finite subgroup check; it is corroboration, not a replacement for the geometric proof.

value.rationale: Tame degree three is the first possible tame gonality for elliptic curves in characteristic two. The necessary-and-sufficient F2 point-count boundary identifies exactly one of five arithmetic forms and explains it by a nontrivial Frobenius descent obstruction. Earlier existence theorems do not distinguish their minimal tame degree. The answer gives structural information useful for explicit Hurwitz loci and arithmetic twists, with limitations openly stated.
